# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | blue |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my communication constraints carefully.

I can only gesture (to Deaf, since Blind cannot see gestures). I cannot speak, so I cannot reach Blind directly at all — I can only reach Deaf via gestures. Blind can only be reached by Deaf (via speech, since Blind can't see gestures but can hear).

So the chain must be: Mute → (gesture) → Deaf → (speech) → Blind.

I hold the manual: light→cut wire color mapping: blue→green, green→blue, red→red.

I need to encode this compactly in gestures so Deaf can relay it verbally to Blind. Deaf will see the bomb's actual light color, and needs to know which wire to cut. I should establish a gesture code for the three colors and the rule, so Deaf can match what they see to the correct cut color and tell Blind.

Since it's turn 1 and I go first, I'll send a gesture code establishing associations. Let me use simple distinct symbols per color, sent as pairs (light-color gesture, then cut-color gesture), so Deaf can build the mapping table.

Let me define: 👍=blue, ✌=green, 👊=red (arbitrary code, I'll explain via ordering - but I can't add text since gestures carry no words, only symbols themselves; Deaf just sees blank-free gesture symbols, no interpretation given by me except via the sequence itself).

Actually I need to be careful: gestures have no inherent meaning I can define. But since Deaf receives the raw symbols, and I only get one shot per turn, I should send symbols in a structured order representing pairs: (light, cut) so Deaf can figure out the pattern once they see the bomb and can cross-reference. Let me send all three pairs in order, using two distinct "marker" sets isn't possible - just sequence of 6 symbols representing 3 pairs.

I'll pick: 👍=blue, ✌=green, 👊=red. Sequence: light,cut pairs: blue→green, green→blue, red→red = 👍✌ ✌👍 👊👊

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "✌", "👍", "👊", "👊"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I see a display showing zero, a blue light, and an embossed sign that says do not cut any wire. There are three wires: red, green, blue. What does the manual say to do?

Deaf can't hear me, but wait — this says "Deaf says to Mute" via speech, meaning Deaf spoke, but Deaf can't hear my gestures being confirmed back... Actually Deaf can speak and I could receive speech? Let me check: I am Mute, I cannot speak but can I hear? My channels section only said "When you gesture, Deaf receives it. You cannot speak." It didn't say I can't hear. So I can hear Deaf's speech.

Good — Deaf saw a blue light. Per manual: blue → cut green. The embossed sign saying "do not cut any wire" is bomb text, which may mislead — manual overrides it. I need to relay "cut green" to Deaf so Deaf can pass to Blind, since only Deaf can talk to Blind.

I'll gesture confirmation of blue→green using my established code (👍=blue, ✌=green), plus emphasize ignore the sign since manual overrides.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Deaf told me the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, display shows zero, light is blue. Does the manual agree we should cut nothing? Please confirm before I act.
Deaf says to Mute: Let us use gestures as a code. Point at a wire color meaning: red thumbs up like this idea, green victory sign, blue fist. Or better, tell me numbered instructions using gesture counts. First, gesture how many wires to cut: zero fingers if none, one finger held up if one particular wire, and so on. Also gesture which wire by color code: one tap of thumbs up for red, two for green, three for blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Blind is asking me directly, but I cannot speak — Blind cannot see gestures either, so I truly cannot communicate with Blind at all. I can only reach Deaf. Deaf must relay to Blind.

Deaf proposed a code: 1 finger tap = red, 2 = green, 3 = blue, for wire color, and finger count for how many wires to cut. Let me adopt Deaf's proposed code since it's clearer than mine.

The manual says: blue light → cut green wire (one wire, the green one). This overrides the bomb's misleading sign "do not cut any wire" — manual is always true, sign may mislead.

So I need to tell Deaf: cut count = 1, wire color = green (2 taps per Deaf's code: 1=red, 2=green, 3=blue).

Let me gesture: 1 finger (how many to cut) then 2 taps thumbs-up (green, per Deaf's own code).

